source: lets make a mech combat game, first person. use generate_mesh to generate the hud. include weapons like gatling guns, rockets, etc... generate a map / terrain. use generate_mesh for trees and other doodads to make an interesting terrain

image_prompt.text: Clusters of trees, boulders and other doodads distributed across the battlefield as cover between mechs
Rugged terrain with varied elevation - hills, rocky outcrops and open flat stretches - sized for mech movement

notes: No preset fitted: the prompt names no mode, so Battle Royale would have injected a shrinking boundary and loot, and Team Deathmatch would have forced a lane network onto terrain the user asked to be open and irregular.
Cover sizes in cover-los are avatar-scale (3-4 and 7-8 studs) and are wrong for mechs; the text was kept but the numbers should not be.
The HUD, the cockpit view and the weapon loadout are not layout - logged as gaps.

open_questions.ask: No theme was stated - should the battlefield read as clean sci-fi, grimy industrial war-torn, or something else?
What is the mode - team deathmatch, free-for-all, objective capture, or PvE waves?
How big is a mech relative to an avatar? That decides whether the map is 500 or 5000 studs across.

coverage_missing.ask: Sci-fi neon, military drab, or post-apocalyptic ruin?
Mech size and speed, since the whole map scale hangs off it
Is this PvP against other mechs or PvE against AI?

answers.ask: No theme was stated - should the battlefield read as clean sci-fi, grimy industrial war-torn, or something else?
answers.answer: Use a grimy industrial, war-torn sci-fi battlefield.

answers.ask: What is the mode - team deathmatch, free-for-all, objective capture, or PvE waves?
answers.answer: Make it a simple free-for-all combat mode to keep the first version focused on mech fighting.

answers.ask: How big is a mech relative to an avatar? That decides whether the map is 500 or 5000 studs across.
answers.answer: Mechs should be about 3x an avatar’s height; use a compact roughly 500-stud battlefield.
